## Severity: P2 (downgraded from filed P0)

## Context

R1 audit originally flagged this as P0 because of an assumed unbounded write path. On re-audit it was downgraded to P2 — the path IS clamped server-side, but the client allows entry of nonsensical values (e.g., 50,000 kcal target) and the server silently clamps without informing the user.

## Finding

Macro target screen accepts arbitrary numeric input. `POST /api/macros/targets` clamps to a sane range (e.g., 500–15000 kcal) but returns 200 with the clamped value, and the client doesn't reconcile the displayed value with the server response. User sees "Saved" then their entered number, but next screen load shows the clamped number — feels like a silent rewrite.

## Fix sketch

- **Client:** enforce min/max in the input control with helper text.
- **Or server:** return 400 with explicit `clamped_to` field; client surfaces "We adjusted X to Y because Z."

## Acceptance

No silent server-side clamping; user always sees what was actually persisted.

## Source

R1 audit, P0→P2 downgrade rationale in verdict file. See `p0_claims_audit_report.md` referenced in `HANDOFF_OP_50.md`.

## Origin

Filed as part of the Operator-49 → Operator-50 R81-backfill P2 batch (mobile track). See `handoffs/quality-bar-raise/current-state.json` `session_findings_to_file[R1-P0-3]` for telemetry pointer.
title: [P2] Macro target inputs lack server-side validation when client sends out-of-range values
